title: Tips to get Claude to make a 3D character actually look like a human?
author: KEEPCARLM
selftext:
I'm making a football(soccer) game where you just take the set-pieces.  Nothing special, but one of the problems I've got is the characters it builds just look so so so bad, like, not even passably bad in a stylistic way.  Just plain bad.

The character models just need to be really basic, low poly human shaped.  I'm getting the weirdest looking models.

Heres what I have https://i.postimg.cc/jSph04jS/unnamed-(2).jpg

I've tried and wasted so much usage credit trying to get something that looks remotely human shaped...  I considered getting something ready made to implement in the game, but adding the data into the html file the game is in just bloats the file size and then I run out of 'chat size' and i can't process any further requests.

Is there something I can do to help?   I've tried sending reference images of what I want, I've tried explaining it, I've even tried asking Kimi to have a go (Kimi made them look like Minecraft characters haha).  I've had them rebuilt from scratch and all sorts, they are just always really disappointing.

comments.author: Cubey42
comments.body: Unlikely you're gonna get a good result on opus. I was doing some interesting things in fable but that was too short lived to know for sure.

replies.author: KEEPCARLM
replies.body: Yeah unfortunately  I missed fable being open

replies.author: knight1b
replies.body: Even fable isn't likely to get this result you will need something more specialized.

comments.author: Smilysis
comments.body: Why are you using a llm to create game models while there are already extremely capable ai models (which you can eve run locally) for 3D work? xd

replies.author: KEEPCARLM
replies.body: because, like I said - if I implement a true 3D model into the HTML file, the amount of code balloons

replies.author: Smilysis
replies.body: You're already vibecoding the whole thing, why are you even putting everything in a single file when game engines with good mcp connectors exist?

replies.author: KEEPCARLM
replies.body: correct, that is why I am asking for advice rather than telling other people how to do it lol

replies.author: Smilysis
replies.body:
and i literally told you to either use a 3d model or a game engine and yet you still want to do everything in a single markdown file which was not designed neither made for game development

it's either this or your learn how to code and make your own model in three.js (which would literally take up the same ammount of effort to just using a 3D model XD)

replies.author: KEEPCARLM
replies.body: appreciate you are giving me good advice, but no need to be so weird about it.

comments.author: samuele_v
comments.body:
Something that I found works well with VFX effects and such, so it might also work for your issue (or not) - try literally directing it to search on the Web for guides/tutorials on how to create \[what you want to create\].  
  
I found that it systematically produces better outputs than anything it would do on its own or following my own explanations.

replies.author: KEEPCARLM
replies.body: I will give this a go, thanks.

comments.author: teamharder
comments.body: Check out Meshy. It's gotten decent. Free tier basically let's you test out creating and rigging 3 models.

comments.author: Hour-Dragonfly-7499
comments.body:
Why not just use free 3d models? there's tons of low poly human models you can use and change them to your liking.

AI is used to assist you but you still need to put in work, there's blender you could learn and blender MCP [https://github.com/ahujasid/blender-mcp](https://github.com/ahujasid/blender-mcp)

comments.author: Calm_Pass_4289
comments.body: no. learn to sculpt or hire an artist. ai cant even get close to proper form and topology. it will fail everytime due to how complex the shapes are...and even then could flag you for inappropriate content.
